name: New York Control to Zombie
summary: Zombie is the hand-clearing pummel from Mission Control into New York; it is needed again only if the opponent has recovered the arm inside.
description: New York Control to Zombie revisits the hand-clearing pummel only if the opponent recovers an inside arm. Preserve Mission Control while rebuilding the knee hug.
overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York Control, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Completed New York already contains the result of the Zombie pummel. First recognize a lost arm isolation and re-establish Mission Control rather than treating Zombie as a later static lockdown.

Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward. Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

attacker.description: New York Control to Zombie (attacker): Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward.
attacker.overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York Control, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Completed New York already contains the result of the Zombie pummel. First recognize a lost arm isolation and re-establish Mission Control rather than treating Zombie as a later static lockdown.

Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward. Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.

Cover the cleared arm and close the knee hug as the hand reaches the mat. Once the arm is isolated, maintain that new control instead of repeatedly treating Zombie as a separate leg entanglement. Keep a safe guard and look for another opening when the opponent maintains inside frames.

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): When is another Zombie pummel actually needed?
flashcards.answer: Completed New York already contains the cleared arm. Re-pummel only if that isolation is lost and the hand comes back inside.
flashcards.answer_line: After their hand has recovered to an inside frame

plausible: While the cleared hand remains outside the knee hug
When the second leg reinforces an already isolated arm
trap: After the controlling arm clears the head but the overhook stays intact

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): Which control must survive while your free hand works?
flashcards.answer: Restore Mission Control posture control before using the free hand for the renewed pummel.
flashcards.answer_line: A supported high leg holding posture down

plausible: Only a low ankle cross with posture upright
Both hands chasing the wrist with no leg support
trap: A high ankle hold with the knee drifting away

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): In Eddy's hand-first version, where do you enter?
flashcards.answer: Ben Eddy works under the hand rather than trying to pry beneath the strongly clamped elbow; this is one demonstrated version.
flashcards.answer_line: Under the hand through the available opening

plausible: Directly under the tightly clamped elbow
Over the wrist, pressing it back toward the chest
trap: Under the elbow first, then forward toward the hand

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): What should you guide as the pummel clears the frame?
flashcards.answer: Move the arm through available space and guide the hand outside, rather than manipulating individual fingers.
flashcards.answer_line: The wrist and forearm toward the mat

plausible: The elbow straight outward while the wrist stays on the chest
The hand straight upward while its elbow remains inside
trap: The wrist toward your centerline beneath their chest

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): What follows as the hand reaches the mat?
flashcards.answer: The cleared hand must be followed by the arm wrap and supported knee hug to restore New York isolation.
flashcards.answer_line: Cover the arm and close the knee hug

plausible: Leave the elbow uncovered while switching grips
Keep the hand outside with a wrist grip but no knee hug
trap: Change the head-side grip before covering the cleared elbow

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): The hand is cleared and the knee hugged; what now?
flashcards.answer: Once the hand-clearing goal is reached, retain the resulting control rather than repeating an unnecessary pummel.
flashcards.answer_line: Maintain the recovered New York arm isolation

plausible: Pummel again around the arm already held outside
Release the knee hug to let the cleared hand return inside
trap: Replace the supported high shin with crossed ankles at the waist

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): Their inside frame remains strong; what is the fallback?
flashcards.answer: If the hand path remains closed, maintain safe guard structure rather than forcing the tightly clamped elbow outward.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep guard and wait for another hand opening

plausible: Open both legs and keep reaching for the elbow
Reach behind their back with both arms
trap: Keep reaching under the clamped elbow after the hand gap shuts

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): If posture also escapes, what takes priority?
flashcards.answer: When both arm isolation and posture control fail, recover the torso barrier before trying another arm trap.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder frame and an inside-knee recovery

plausible: The overhook even while your knees are passed
A high foot grip despite their upright chest
trap: Re-pummel the wrist before replacing the near knee

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): Which observation proves this is a reset, not advancement?
flashcards.answer: New York normally follows Zombie. A renewed Zombie from this node is justified by lost arm isolation, not a later static position.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent had regained their hand inside

plausible: The knee hug remained closed throughout
The head-side arm had already cleared the neck
trap: The free leg had climbed while the trapped hand stayed outside

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (bottom): What should a re-pummel drill end by checking?
flashcards.answer: A cooperative drill confirms the cleared hand and knee hug as the recovered New York connection, without finishing pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Hand outside, arm covered and knee supported

plausible: Only that your pummeling hand moved upward
Only that the opponent lowered their chin
trap: Hand on the mat with the elbow still inside your thigh

defender.description: New York Control to Zombie (defender): Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
defender.overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York Control, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. Completed New York already contains the result of the Zombie pummel. First recognize a lost arm isolation and re-establish Mission Control rather than treating Zombie as a later static lockdown.

Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed. The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.

Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught. Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control. Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Recovering the inside hand creates an early escape from the arm isolation. Maintain your elbow position and watch the second hand before the high guard can re-establish a submission setup; the pummel itself is not a completed joint lock.

Keep elbow and hand connected: Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
Notice the pummel early: The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.
Recover without yanking: Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught.
Rebuild posture gradually: Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control.
Respect the high guard: Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (top): What must your recovered arm retain?
flashcards.answer: After escaping the New York isolation, keep the recovered forearm inside so the bottom player cannot immediately re-pummel.
flashcards.answer_line: An inside forearm with the elbow toward the ribs

plausible: A wide mat post outside their hip
A reach behind their neck with the elbow high
trap: A hand on their chest with the elbow beyond their knee

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (top): How should you avoid leaving the wrist exposed?
flashcards.answer: Move the arm as a coordinated unit; an inside elbow with the hand left outside still gives the pummeler an opening.

plausible: Retract the elbow but leave the hand on the mat
Reach the hand over their shoulder before the elbow returns
trap: Raise the chest to pull the wrist past their high leg

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (top): Which action signals a renewed attempt?
flashcards.answer: Watch the second hand under your recovered hand, because that is the early cue for the renewed hand-clearing pummel.
flashcards.answer_line: Their free hand entering beneath yours

plausible: Their free knee lowering to recover guard
Their legs crossing low around the waist
trap: Their hand moves around your head while the knee hug stays

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (top): When can the elbow be drawn back safely?
flashcards.answer: Use the open path to recover the elbow beside the ribs; do not jerk against a completed arm enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: While the shoulder has slack in the high leg

plausible: Whenever your hand reaches their sternum
Only after pulling the wrist to full extension
trap: When the wrist is loose but their knee hug still clamps the elbow

flashcards.question: New York Control to Zombie (top): What must clear before you raise the chest?
flashcards.answer: Upright posture follows release of the upper-body connection; escaping the hand alone may leave the leg attached.
flashcards.answer_line: The arm trap and attached high-leg control

plausible: Only their pummeling fingertips from your hand
Only their free foot resting against your hip
trap: Only the isolated arm while the high shin still holds your head
